cards.explanation: The answer is by sea in papyrus vessels, friends. The text says this land "…sends couriers by sea, in papyrus vessels on the waters." (Isaiah 18:2) Papyrus boats on the waters means the mail goes out by boat. My cookie boxes only have to cross the counter, so I'm humbled.
The answer is True, friends. The messengers go to "…a people widely feared…" (Isaiah 18:2) The verse also calls them tall, smooth-skinned and a powerful nation. That's a résumé you'd read twice.

The answer is divided by rivers, bakers. The verse says this nation's land is "…divided by rivers." (Isaiah 18:2) It's the same detail the passage repeats in verse 7, so it must matter. Rivers running through the land, like lines of icing on a cookie.

The two answers are see and hear, friends. The text says, "…when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it…" (Isaiah 18:3) A banner is something you look at, and a raised one on a mountain is hard to miss. Then the verse says, "when a ram’s horn sounds, you will hear it." (Isaiah 18:3) A horn is made to be heard, so the verse pairs one thing to look at with one thing to listen to.

The answer is quietly look on, friends. The LORD says, "I will quietly look on from My dwelling place…" (Isaiah 18:4) Notice the word quietly. He looks on from where He dwells, and the verse says it will be quiet.

The answer is True, bakers. The LORD says it is "…like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest." (Isaiah 18:4) Both comparisons are right there in the verse. He gives two pictures for His quiet looking on.

The answer is cut them off with a pruning knife, friends. The text says, "…He will cut off the shoots with a pruning knife…" (Isaiah 18:5) The timing is before the harvest, once the flower has become a ripening grape. It's a picture of a vine being cut back.
The answer is False, friends. The text says He will "…remove and discard the branches." (Isaiah 18:5) Nothing is saved for later. It's a tough picture, and I won't pretend it isn't.

The answer is True, bakers. The text says, "They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey, and to the beasts of the land." (Isaiah 18:6) It goes on to say the birds will feed on them in summer, and all the wild animals in winter. I think this part is heavy, so let's take a breath together.

The answer is gifts, friends! The text says, "At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of Hosts…" (Isaiah 18:7) These gifts come from the same widely feared nation named earlier in the passage. I did NOT see that one coming, and I'm still smiling about it.

The answer is Zion, friends. The gifts go "…to Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the LORD of Hosts." (Isaiah 18:7) The passage ends there, with a destination. A good place to land after all that talk of knives and branches.
